🚑 Account Rescue: When Things Go Wrong · Lesson 4 of 6

Copyright Claims, Strikes & Takedowns: Fix Them Without Losing the Channel

7 min read · Updated November 2026 · Free · Written for Kenya
Share: WhatsApp X Facebook Telegram LinkedIn

On YouTube, writing 'all credit to the artist' doesn't count as a reason to dispute a copyright claim. Neither does owning the song or not monetising the video. And a weak dispute can turn a harmless claim into a strike.

Copyright problems come in two weights. A claim is the rights owner taking the money or muting the sound. A strike is a mark against your account, and enough of them shut it down. Treat them very differently.

3 in 90 days
copyright strikes that make a YouTube channel subject to termination. A strike only expires after 90 days if you've completed Copyright School (YouTube Help: Copyright strike basics)
Platform / situationWhere to respondThe rule that matters
YouTube Content ID claimStudio > Content > Restrictions > See details. Dispute, or remove the claimed audioThe claimant has 30 days to respond. If they reject your appeal, they can file a removal request, and that means a strike.
YouTube copyright strikeCopyright School; ask the claimant to retract; or a counter notificationIf the email says removal is 'scheduled', you have 7 days to delete the video and avoid the strike.
TikTokOpen the flagged video > View copyright details > Appeal. Policy: tiktok.com/legal/page/global/copyright-policy/enBusiness accounts only get the Commercial Music Library. Branded posts count as commercial even on personal accounts.
Instagram & FacebookThe in-app notice, or Settings > Account Status, then appealRepeated IP removals can restrict or disable the account. Keep your licences and original files.
Someone stole YOUR videoYouTube copyright removal request; TikTok form at tiktok.com/legal/report/Copyright; in-app IP report on MetaOnly report what you actually own. False reports carry consequences too.
Kenya (offline)Kenya Copyright Board (KECOBO): copyright.go.keCopyright exists automatically once a work is recorded or written. Registration at nrr.copyright.go.ke is optional evidence.

What to do the day a notice lands

  1. Identify the type. Claim, strike, mute or removal? The fix differs for each.
  2. Be honest about rights. Did you make it, license it, or use the platform's own library for the right account type?
  3. Take the cheap fix first. Trim, mute or swap the claimed song. YouTube lets you remove the claimed content instead of disputing.
  4. Dispute only with proof: a licence, your own original recording, or written permission.
  5. Complete Copyright School if you got a YouTube strike, or the strike won't expire.
  6. Start a rights folder. Keep licences, receipts, producer WhatsApp permissions and raw files with dates.
📋 Dispute text (only when you have the rights)
I have the rights to use the claimed material.
Track/clip: [title, artist/producer]
Basis: [licence from (source), licence ID (number), dated (date), covering online and commercial use] OR [original recording made by me on (date); raw file available]
Claimed segment: [mm:ss to mm:ss]
Supporting proof: [licence PDF / written permission from (name) on (date)]
I'm happy to provide documents on request.
✗ MYTH

If I give credit to the artist, I can use their song.

✓ REALITY

YouTube lists 'giving credit', 'I bought the song' and 'I'm not monetising' as invalid dispute reasons. Credit isn't permission. Use licensed or platform-library music, or get written permission from the artist or producer.

Kenyan copyright basics

  • Automatic protection: your videos, photos, beats and captions are protected from creation. KECOBO says registration is optional, but its certificate helps prove ownership in a dispute.
  • Takedowns through internet providers: the Copyright (Amendment) Act 2019 (section 35B) lets rights owners send takedown notices that providers must act on within 48 business hours, unless they get a counter-notice.
  • False notices are a crime: filing a false or malicious takedown or counter-notice can mean a fine of up to KES 500,000, up to five years in prison, or both.
💡 What most creators miss

Copyright tools built for rights owners are being abused. In August 2026 India's Delhi High Court asked Meta why scammers seemed able to use Rights Manager to file false claims while established creators were refused access. Your best defence is boring: dated original files and a rights folder you can attach to any appeal within minutes.

✅ Do this today
⚡ Quick check

Your YouTube video gets a Content ID claim for a popular Kenyan song. Your description says 'No copyright intended, all credit to the artist'. Is that a valid dispute reason?

YouTube says credit, owning a copy and not monetising aren't valid reasons. If the claimant rejects your appeal they can request removal, and a valid removal request brings a copyright strike.

🧠 Key takeaways
  1. A claim costs money or sound. A strike threatens the account. Three YouTube strikes in 90 days can end a channel.
  2. Remove or swap the claimed audio before you dispute. Only dispute with real proof of rights.
  3. TikTok business accounts are limited to the Commercial Music Library.
  4. In Kenya copyright is automatic, and false takedown notices are a criminal offence.
